title: All Souls' Day
hookLine: on 2 November, Catholics pray for the dead

lines: A BOOK OPEN BY THE DOOR.
cards: A Catholic church on the second of November. Near the door, in some parishes, a book lies open on a stand, and people stop on their way in to write in it. Not messages.
A friend from school. A baby who never came home from the hospital. Later, during Mass, those names are remembered and prayed for.
In some towns, families are already at the cemetery with flowers and candles. The day has a long official name. The short one is All Souls' Day.

teach.b: The Church calendar calls it the Commemoration of All the Faithful Departed, and it comes right after All Saints' Day. All Saints honors the holy ones.
All Souls prays for all the faithful departed, the ordinary dead, the ones people knew. Why pray for them?
Catholics teach that some who die in God's friendship are still being made ready for heaven, a cleansing the Church calls purgatory, and that the prayers of the living can help them.

The text Catholics point to is the second book of Maccabees, where Judas Maccabeus and his men pray for fallen soldiers: "It is therefore a holy and wholesome thought to pray for the dead, that they may be loosed from sins."
Orthodox Christians also pray for the dead, with their own days of remembrance through the year.

Churches shaped by the Reformation generally don't teach purgatory, and their Bibles don't count Maccabees among the books of the Old Testament, though they remember the dead in their own services and prayers.
Nobody needs to settle that today.

teach.h: THE CENTER IS A LIST OF NAMES.
teach.b: Whatever the theology, the center of the day is a list. In parish churches, the old prayer asks for eternal rest and perpetual light for the dead.
A person is remembered not as a number in a cemetery but by the name someone once called across a kitchen.

how: On All Souls' Day Catholics attend Mass for the dead, write names in a parish book of remembrance, visit and tend graves, and light candles; Orthodox Christians keep their own days for praying for the dead.

games.q: you walk into a church on All Souls' Day and see a book open by the door. what do people write in it?
o: their own names, to sign in.
games.why: names: a mother, a brother, a friend. later they're remembered and prayed for at Mass.

practice: Bring to mind someone who has died, family, a friend, a teacher, someone you knew only a little, and give their name one full breath, silently or aloud; if another name comes, give it a breath too.
If no one you knew has died, choose a name you've read on a gravestone or a memorial. If you pray, you can use the old words asking eternal rest and perpetual light for them.

wordCard.voice: Purgatory, the cleansing Catholics teach some souls undergo before heaven, which prayers on All Souls' Day are believed to help. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: by name. Each name on the list carries a whole person with it. Until tomorrow.
